description.value: A modified Experiences Questionnaire measuring in-the-moment state decentering and state rumination while participants reflected on the stressor during the video recovery period. It contained 17 items rated from 1 (not at all) to 5 (very much), with 11 decentering items and 6 rumination items; reliability was α=0.704 and α=0.662, respectively.

spans.text: The decentering questionnaire was based on the experiences questionnaire ( Fresco   et al.  , 2007 ) and consisted of two factors: rumination and decentering. We modified the items to measure in-the-moment stressor experience (state rumination and state decentering). Specifically, the participants were instructed to think about how much they endorsed those thoughts while watching the video, such as ‘I had the sense that I was fully aware of what was going on around me and inside me’. The 17 items were rated on a scale from 1 (‘not at all’) to 5 (‘very much’). In this sample, both subscales had acceptable reliability (state decentering: 11 items; α = 0.704; state rumination: 6 items; α = 0.662).

model_settings.value: Baseline activation was subtracted from stressor and recovery activation. Exponentially weighted moving-average z values were calculated at each post-baseline time point and analyzed with hierarchical EWMA models. Regressors were median-split and mean-centered for group analyses; change points required three consecutive above-threshold time points, followed by 2D spatial-temporal k-means clustering with k≥10, FWE correction over time, and retention of clusters with at least one FDR q<0.05 peak. Cluster activation was summarized using a voxel-above-threshold ratio greater than 0.05 and participant-level weighted regression.
